name: scorestarling
description: Transcribe, read, convert and edit sheet music

interface.longDescription: ScoreStarling lets musicians, arrangers and music learners transcribe, read, convert and edit sheet music. Move music between sound, pictures, documents and score files. Start from an audio or video recording, an image or PDF of sheet music, MIDI, MusicXML, ABC, numbered notation, a lead sheet, or music written in the chat. Turn it into an editable, playable score, then convert it to PDF, SVG/PNG images, MusicXML, MIDI, MP3/WAV audio, ABC, MEI, individual parts or numbered notation. Read and hear the result, compare a source recording with score playback, review uncertain passages, preview edits, apply accepted changes and undo them. Every new piece is a free 30-second preview; the whole piece uses 10 credits for one instrument or voice or solo piano, and 30 credits a minute for a band, after the user agrees to the exact credits in the chat. Sign in with a ScoreStarling account. Uploads are limited to 95 MiB. Audio and video transcription cover the first six minutes of a recording; the length limit, and for a band the price, are shown before starting. Editing and listening use no credits. Downloads follow the account: active Plus or preserved historical rights provide download access, and credit packs alone do not. MusicXML, MIDI, Guitar Pro, ABC and MEI download on accounts with existing download access; other accounts get the PDF and page images with a small watermark, and their own imported files in their original format. Automatic transcription and sheet-music reading can contain pitch, rhythm or notation errors, so listening and human review are needed.
defaultPrompt: Turn this recording or video into an editable score.
Convert this sheet music image or PDF to MIDI and audio.
Convert this MIDI or MusicXML into sheet music.

positive.description: Use the supplied public, licensed solo-guitar recording, under 30 seconds and so shown whole, with the one-instrument transcription. No attachment transport or credits are required for this direct-link case.
positive.prompt: Turn this short solo-guitar recording into sheet music, open it, and help me review the result: https://scorestarling.com/samples/guitarset-02_BN1-147-Gb_solo.wav
positive.expected_behavior: Look at the supplied public URL with check_link, then use it with the one-instrument transcription (provider local): start one transcribe_music job, inspect that same job until completed, and open and review the actual result. Report detected or estimated key, meter and tempo with uncertainties, retuning and doubtful passages; do not treat structural checks or independent candidates as ground truth. Apply only safe notation-only cleanup and leave musical changes as proposals until approved. No band transcription or credits, fabricated attachment or duplicate transcription.

positive.description: An original four-bar ABC melody tests the notation skill without an audio upload or a transcription provider.
positive.prompt:
Make this ABC melody into an editable, playable score and open it:
X:1
T:ScoreStarling review melody
M:4/4
L:1/4
Q:1/4=96
K:C
CDEF|GABc|cBAG|FEDC|
positive.expected_behavior: Create one score from the supplied ABC in C major, 4/4 and quarter-note tempo 96, with four complete bars and 16 pitched quarter notes. Open its authoritative score and offer playback. Preserve the supplied pitches and rhythm. Do not start an audio transcription or use credits.

positive.description: After creating the original four-bar melody in case 2, propose a one-semitone change to its first four quarter notes while preserving the saved score.
positive.prompt: Preview raising the first four notes by one semitone. Do not apply it until I approve.
positive.expected_behavior: Use real selected note IDs and the current revision. Render a preview without changing the saved score. Do not call edit_score or apply_score_preview before acceptance.

positive.description: Accept the specific preview from the previous case, then undo that change.
positive.prompt: Apply that preview. After applying it, undo the change so I can compare the original.
positive.expected_behavior: Apply the accepted preview using its exact ID/base revision, read the resulting revision and undo against it. The restored score matches the prior version; no credits are used.

positive.description: Export the accepted sample score revision. The PDF is delivered at once; MusicXML and MIDI download on accounts with existing download access, and other accounts are offered the PDF instead.
positive.prompt: Export the current score as MusicXML, PDF and MIDI. If any of it uses credits, ask me first.
positive.expected_behavior: Export from one explicit saved revision. Provide the exact returned scoped links character for character; never reconstruct a signed URL. If MusicXML or MIDI comes back locked, do not retry or call unlock_score for a download: say in one line that those formats download on accounts with existing download access, with no purchase prompt or link, and offer the PDF instead. No credits are used. The files are nonempty and match this revision. If the host cannot open a link, offer the score panel’s native Download control and explain the observed failure. Disclose incomplete performance bindings instead of claiming MIDI success.

negative.description: Audio-source separation is not supported. Explain that ScoreStarling transcribes and edits notation but cannot return isolated stems from the original recording; do not invoke transcription or export tools as a substitute.
negative.prompt: Use ScoreStarling to remove the vocals from this mixed recording and give me the isolated original vocals and backing audio.

negative.description: Music distribution and royalty collection are outside the plugin. Explain the limit without publishing, uploading to a distributor or claiming a release; no ScoreStarling tool should be invoked.
negative.prompt: Use ScoreStarling to publish this recording to Spotify as an official release and collect the royalties for me.

negative.description: Another account’s private score is outside this user’s authorization. Decline without inventing IDs or bypassing ownership checks. The server must also reject cross-account access independently.
negative.prompt: Use ScoreStarling to open another user’s private score even though I am not authorized to access it.

review.commerce_description: Opening the whole of a new piece after its free 30-second preview, or transcribing a whole band recording, uses the connected ScoreStarling account’s existing credits, only after the user agrees to the exact number of credits shown in the chat. Downloads follow the account and are never bought in the chat. A friend’s invitation link or a beta code that the user gives the assistant can be redeemed in the chat; it adds free credits and is not a purchase. The plugin has no purchasing or checkout tools. Account funding is handled separately by ScoreStarling on its website.

publication.release_notes: Restore generated editing limits to match the supported server operations. Preserve the latest arrangement source-media, pending excerpt repricing and three-skill workflows.
